newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, E.Europe farm ministers to discuss vet rules.
newsitem.headline: EU, E.Europe farm ministers to discuss vet rules.

text.p: European Union farm ministers will hold a third meeting with prospective east European members on Tuesday to discuss adapting veterinary and plant health rules to meet EU standards, EU officials said.

In view of the mad cow crisis, recent outbreaks of swine fever and foot and mouth disease, member states are concerned that the new east European members should be able to enforce EU food safety standards.

The east European countries will be also responsible for applying EU controls on imports of cattle, meat and other veterinary and plant products from the former Soviet Union and other eastern suppliers.
Mutual confidence and recognition of the competence of the veterinary authorities in the applicant countries must be established, officials said.
There is also EU public concern about disparities in animal welfare rules, such as the protection of animals during long journeys and slaughtering standards.

Poland, Hungary and the Czech republic are expected to be among the first to join the EU early next century. Slovakia, Romania, Bulgaria, Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia and Slovenia have also applied to join.
